cells.tense: Right now you are holding what needs holding without squeezing it shut.
cells.act: sit with someone in it without fixing it
cells.ask: Next time someone close is in something hard, stay there with them a few minutes and offer nothing that fixes it — no advice, no bright side.
cells.core:
You're in a stretch where you can stand beside someone in something hard and not require it to move. You feel what they're carrying without either of you vanishing into the other. Not many people can do that quietly, and the ones close to you can feel when you're doing it.

One more thing this balance is free to feed: staying near while it stays hard. Sit with them, bring nothing that solves it, and don't rush to fill the quiet. That doesn't load them up, and it doesn't take you under either. What the two of you find in that time isn't something either of you could have made alone.
cells.sheetLine: You can hold someone without crushing them or being crushed.
cells.verb: Bearing what has to be held.
cells.place: In the room where you feel what others feel, alongside them.

cells.tense: You're gripping the thing before the moment gets here.
cells.act: let an exchange flow both ways
cells.ask: Where you carry the whole load for someone, give back a piece that's theirs and let a piece of yours be carried by them.
cells.core:
When it's going well, you stand beside someone and let what they feel move through you without either of you disappearing. That's still in you. But lately you're bracing for what hasn't arrived. What was steady bearing has turned into carrying everything — every tension around you — so the next hard feeling finds you already tight. It's harder to sit with anyone while your hands are full. Keep going this way and you'll do the one thing that would hurt: stop letting anyone reach you.

Let the weight move both directions. Give back something you've been carrying for someone else, then say something you're carrying to whoever can take it. One in, one out, nothing settled. A balance you keep calculating stops being flow.
cells.sheetLine: Holding everything makes it harder to feel what you're holding.
cells.verb: Bearing what has to be held.
cells.place: In the room where you feel what others feel, alongside them.

cells.tense: The place where you feel what others feel is still waiting at a door that closed already.
cells.act: put it down and leave your hands empty a while
cells.ask: Set down the weight you still carry for someone who no longer needs it, and leave an afternoon this week unclaimed.
cells.core:
The flatness you're in has a shape: an old defense still up, and the room where this strength lives still waiting at a boundary that moved on. You hold from behind a shield now. When the moment comes to be with someone in what they're feeling, hands that are too full can't reach.

Releasing works where pushing doesn't. Set a held weight down — a routine kept out of habit, a burden that belongs to someone else now — and leave an afternoon empty. Nothing gets handed over, nothing gets accomplished. Empty hands are the first thing that makes contact possible again.
cells.sheetLine: Put down what you still carry, then let your hands be empty.
cells.verb: Bearing what has to be held.
cells.place: In the room where you feel what others feel, alongside them.

cells.tense: You're holding people up right now, and you'd say it was just the circumstances.
cells.act: move toward the thing you actually want
cells.ask: Spend an hour this week moving toward something you want that has nothing to do with what anyone needs from you.
cells.core:
You have been the steady one for people going through it — the one who could stand in the middle of the mess and not break. You call that being around. That isn't something in the air; it's your strength, being used. Nobody asked you to name it, so you haven't.

Before you were carrying them, you had a pull of your own — something you wanted for yourself. Get near it again, an hour or so, long enough to remember the feel of it. This isn't a duty. It's the thing that was drawing you before anyone needed you to hold them up.
cells.sheetLine: What they lean on is yours. Take an hour back.
cells.verb: Bearing what has to be held.
cells.place: In the room where you feel what others feel, alongside them.
